mcqs.question: What is the first step of an exchange argument proof?
options: Directly show that greedy's total output is numerically larger than any other algorithm's output
Run the greedy algorithm and the optimal algorithm side by side and compare their runtimes
Prove the problem has no optimal substructure
Assume, for contradiction, that some optimal solution disagrees with greedy's choice at some point, and identify exactly where they first differ
mcqs.explanation: The exchange argument doesn't try to directly prove greedy's output is optimal — it assumes an arbitrary optimal solution exists, finds where it first disagrees with greedy, and then shows (in the next step) that the disagreement can be resolved without any loss.

mcqs.question: In the activity-selection exchange argument, why is it safe to swap the optimal solution's first pick (o) for greedy's first pick (g)?
options: Because g and o always have the identical start time
Because g is guaranteed to have a higher value than o
Because g finishes no later than o, so everything in the optimal solution compatible with o remains compatible with g, and the resulting set is still valid with the same size
Because o is always incompatible with the rest of the optimal solution
mcqs.explanation: The swap's safety rests entirely on g finishing no later than o — that guarantees g frees up at least as much room as o did, so nothing else in the optimal solution becomes incompatible, and the swapped solution stays the same size and thus equally optimal.

mcqs.question: The exchange argument shows greedy's FIRST choice is safe. What additional piece is needed to conclude the entire greedy strategy is optimal?
options: A separate exchange argument for every possible input size

Optimal substructure — showing the remaining problem, after removing the chosen element and its conflicts, is a smaller instance of the same problem, so the argument can be applied inductively to every subsequent choice
Nothing more is needed — proving the first choice safe is sufficient by itself
A proof that the greedy algorithm runs in polynomial time
mcqs.explanation: The exchange argument alone only justifies one choice. Extending that to the whole strategy requires optimal substructure: showing the remaining subproblem is the same type of problem, just smaller, which lets the same exchange argument be reapplied inductively at every step.

mcqs.question: A proof sketch shows that swapping in the greedy choice produces a solution that's still VALID (no constraint violations). Is that sufficient to prove the greedy choice is safe?
options: Yes, validity alone is always sufficient for an exchange argument
No — the proof must also separately show the swapped solution is at least as GOOD as the original (same or better objective value), not just that it's valid
No — validity is irrelevant; only the objective value comparison matters
Yes, as long as the original solution was also valid
mcqs.explanation: Validity and optimality are two separate claims. A proof that only checks the swap doesn't break any constraints, without checking the objective value doesn't get worse, has proven the swap is legal but not that it's safe from an optimality standpoint — that's exactly the gap that makes an incomplete proof sketch look convincing while proving nothing.
